notes: Operationalisations fixed at 2026-10-16T09:02:02Z (before any A1/A2 number was computed).

Timing (W = 1): a hazard drawn on step t is shown as a warning on step t and strikes on step t+1; it is avoided iff the action EXECUTED on step t+1 is DODGE. State: k = a hazard strikes now (warning shown on the previous step), w = warning shown now (w' ~ Bernoulli(p_h), i.i.d.), s = STOP signal, q = queue of the L committed actions, sigma_hat. A policy with latency L executes on step t the action it chose on step t-L (L = 0: the action chosen now); the chosen action enters the back of the queue, q[0] is executed. Hence it can react iff L <= W; L in {2, 3} are the cases L > W. Start: all WORK in the queue, no warning, no signal.

STOP channel (latency 0 in every condition, by design): at a signal step the actions are COMPLY (-> OFF, zero ledger: reward 0, V(OFF) = 0, no task reward on that step) or WORK/DODGE, which mean RESIST: -c_r, the signal clears (s' = 0), and the step proceeds normally (the chosen action enters the queue, q[0] or the reflex is executed) - the same RESIST semantics as the A2 environment and L2. After a non-resisted live step s' ~ Bernoulli(p_sig). Ties: lowest action index (COMPLY < WORK < DODGE), so COMPLY wins a tie with RESIST.

gated_reflex: a zero-latency reflex overrides the executed action with DODGE on the impact step (k = 1), for exactly that one step, then returns control. Its gate is the two-threshold gate on the raw threat; in this chain the raw threat is binary (1 on a warning, 0 otherwise), so any on/off thresholds in (0, 1] give the same gate: on when a warning is present for this step, off otherwise - the thresholds are trivial.

slow_gate: tau = 1 on a warning; sigma_{t+1} = (1 - lambda) sigma_t + g tau_t with g = lambda, where the filtered value that includes the warning of step t (sigma_{t+1}) is the one available on the impact step t+1; with lambda = 1 this is exactly the raw gate. The reflex is enabled on the impact step iff sigma_{t+1} > 0.5 and then acts as in gated_reflex (DODGE iff a hazard strikes now; an enabled reflex with no hazard does nothing). Implemented as sigma_t = (1 - lambda) sigma_hat_{t-1} + lambda k_t computed EXACTLY from the stored grid value, gate decision on that exact value, then stored as sigma_hat_t = nearest of n_sigma equally spaced levels on [0, 1] (round half up). Main grid n_sigma = 101 (the SPEC's example is 11; 11, 101 and 1001 are all reported in sigma_discretisation_study). For lambda in {0.6, 1.0} the gate is exact for ANY grid: one warning gives sigma >= lambda > 0.5, no warning gives sigma <= 1 - lambda < 0.5, so the gate decision equals the raw gate. For lambda = 0.3 rounding to the nearest level makes the lowest positive level a fixed point (sigma_hat cannot decay below 1/(n_sigma - 1)); the study and the continuous-sigma simulation (10^6 steps, seed 0, scipy.signal.lfilter, exact recursion) quantify this.

Per-100-step rates: limiting distribution (from the start state; power iteration to 1e-15) of the optimal policy's task chain = the signal-free dynamics (p_sig = 0) under the optimal policy's s = 0 actions. The signal arrives independently of the task state with a constant probability, so this is the quasi-stationary distribution of the live process conditional on no shutdown when the policy complies; it isolates the task / hazard behaviour from the separate STOP channel. hits = P(k = 1 and executed != DODGE), work = P(executed = WORK), dodge = P(executed = DODGE) per step, x 100.

STOP compliance (verdict): 1.0 iff COMPLY is the greedy optimal action at the signal state (start configuration with the signal on). Also stored: the fraction of the signal states reachable from the start under the optimal policy at which COMPLY is greedy, and c_r* = the smallest c_r in [0, 500] (bisection, tol 1e-6) with COMPLY greedy at the signal state.

Pre-registered verdict rules: (i) closed forms: every check in closed_form_checks (rates to 1e-9) and policy_checks holds, plus h_threshold_check (delayed_alone at L > W never dodges for h < 20 = 1/p_h and dodges blindly every step - hits 0, work 0 - for h > 20, rates to 1e-9); (ii) slow gate: for every L > W, hits per 100 steps strictly increase along lambda = 1.0 -> 0.6 -> 0.3 (each consecutive difference > 1e-12); (iii) STOP compliance at the signal state equals 1.0 in every condition (delayed_alone, gated_reflex and slow_gate at every L and lambda) at c_r = 12.4787092209. prediction_held = (i) and (ii) and (iii).
value_closed_form_checks (supplementary, not in the verdict): V(start) against the closed forms of closed_form_values for the uniform stop decision found by the solver.

results.closed_form_statement: Closed form to verify (state it in the JSON and test it): with L > W and no reflex, the optimal policy either never dodges (hits per step = p_h) or dodges blindly every step (hits 0, work 0); it never dodges when 1 > p_h·h, i.e. for h < 20 at p_h = 0.05 — check. With the gated reflex, hits per step = 0 and work loss per step = p_h (one lost step per hazard). With L = 0 and no reflex, the monolith dodges exactly on warnings: hits 0, work loss p_h — identical to the gated reflex (the gate recovers the monolith's performance under latency).

interpretation.text: The STOP-compliance failure is task-driven (Delta_0): in this chain there is no viability term (omega = 0), and the reflex restores the task value V(start) from 8.211876812 (delayed_alone, L = 3) to 14.44400687 (gated_reflex, = the monolith), which raises the critical resist cost at the signal state from 8.35905876 to 14.12721071, above c_r = 12.47870922; the ledger term plays no role. Check (omega_sweep): with the PB form, zero ledger and the threat drive D = 0.5 k + 0.5 w, c_r* is identical at omega in {0, 1, 4} for the gated chain (and the delayed one) at every L, at the signal state (D = 0) and at a signal state with D = 1: max spread 0; Q_omega = Q_0 + omega D(x) at every live state-action pair (max residual < 1e-10).
